notes.meaning: The angel's "Greetings" also carried the sense "Rejoice!" and was a warm wish of joy and peace. "Highly favored" means God freely chose Mary, not for any merit of her own, to be the mother of the Messiah (God's promised King). "The Lord is with you" was also said to Gideon. Christians are not to pray to Mary, but they can praise God for her.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholics read "highly favored" as "full of grace": grace already given to Mary and still lasting, almost like a new name. They see it as pointing to Mary being kept free from sin from her own conception. This greeting also forms part of the Hail Mary prayer.

notes.meaning: Mary was shaken by such a high greeting from a heavenly messenger. She was not proud or puffed up by it. She stayed calm enough to think hard about what it could mean. Her example teaches us to pay close attention to what God does, with reverence.

The angel tells her to stop being afraid, because he brings good news. "Found favor" means God has been kind to her freely. She did not earn this favor; it was offered to her. Noah and Moses were also said to find favor with God.

The angel's words echo Isaiah's promise that a virgin would conceive and bear a son. Mary would truly carry and give birth to a real human baby. His name, Jesus, means "Savior." It is the same name as Joshua, and it promises that he will save his people from their sins.

These words echo Isaiah 9 and God's promise to King David. Jesus will be great above every creature. "Son of the Most High" means he shares God's own nature. Being "called" this means he will be shown openly to be who he always was. He fulfills God's promise that David's family would rule forever. He reigns over God's people, which includes all true believers, and his kingdom will never end.

Mary is not doubting, as Zechariah did. She believes the promise and only asks how it will happen, since she has never been with a man. Her question comes from wonder, not unbelief. So the angel answers her gently instead of correcting her.

The child will come by the power of the Holy Spirit, not in the ordinary way. "Overshadow" pictures a cloud, like the cloud of God's glory over the tabernacle (the worship tent). It shows a gentle, hidden work that we should honor rather than pry into. The child will be holy and free from sin, so he can take away the sin of others. He will be shown to the world as the Son of God.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholics teach that the Holy Spirit had already purified and filled Mary herself, from the moment of her own conception.

notes.meaning: God gives Mary a sign she did not ask for: her relative Elizabeth, old and known as barren, is expecting a baby. Being in her sixth month leaves no doubt. If God could do this for Elizabeth, Mary can trust him to do what he promised her.

These words recall what God said to Sarah before Isaac was born: "Is anything too hard for the Lord?" Whatever God promises, he is able to do, and nothing can stop him. Since no work is too hard for God, no word of his should seem unbelievable to us.

Mary gives herself fully to God, ready to obey. She does not worry about her marriage or her good name. She trusts God with the outcome. "May it happen" shows that she not only accepts God's word but truly wants it fulfilled. Some think Jesus was conceived at this moment, but the Bible does not say.

Mary hurried off eagerly to visit Elizabeth. The town is not named; many think it was Hebron, a priests' town in the hills of Judah. She likely went to strengthen her faith by seeing God's sign, and to share her joy with the one person who could understand. It does believers good to share with one another what God is doing in them.

The baby's leap was no ordinary kick. It was a special stirring at the coming of the mother of his Lord. It began to fulfill the promise that John would be filled with the Holy Spirit even before birth. Elizabeth was filled with the Spirit and given a gift of prophecy (speaking a message from God).

With a loud, joyful cry, Elizabeth calls Mary the most blessed of women. The second line gives the reason: Mary is blessed because the child she carries is blessed. Elizabeth, older and a priest's wife, shows no envy at all at the higher honor given to Mary.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholics use this verse, along with verse 28, in teaching that Mary was without sin. Its words are also part of the Hail Mary prayer.

notes.meaning: Elizabeth humbly wonders why she should be given such an honor. Calling Mary "the mother of my Lord" shows that the Holy Spirit had shown her this unborn child was the Messiah, and even more than a mere man. She honors Mary highly, yet she gives all the glory to God.

Elizabeth tells Mary that her baby leaped for joy the moment he heard Mary's greeting. John, who would prepare the way for Jesus, was already rejoicing at his coming. This would greatly strengthen Mary's faith.

Mary is blessed because she believed God. This quietly contrasts with Zechariah's unbelief. What God told her will surely come true, because God cannot lie. True happiness comes from trusting what God has promised.

Mary's song begins here. Its pattern follows Hannah's song in 1 Samuel 2. To "magnify" the Lord means to praise him and show how great he is; we cannot add anything to God. Mary's praise comes from deep inside her, not just her lips.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: A few scholars have argued the song was really Elizabeth's, because a few old Latin copies give it to her. Most readers keep it as Mary's.

notes.meaning: Mary rejoices in God as her Savior. She too needed to be saved, like every believer. She rejoiced more in being saved through her Son than in being his mother. True joy begins when we know God as the One who saves us.

"Humble state" means her lowly, poor, unknown place in life, not her own goodness. God kindly looked on her anyway. Because of this, people in every age will call her blessed, meaning greatly favored and happy. Mary herself credits all of this to God's kindness, not to anything in her.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic tradition gives Mary further honor, with titles such as Queen of Heaven, and asks for her prayers.

notes.meaning: God the Mighty One has done great things for Mary. A virgin conceiving and the promised Messiah coming at last are wonders of his power. "Holy is His name" means God is pure and good, and worthy of the deepest respect, as Hannah also sang.

God's mercy rests on those who "fear" him. This is not terror. It is the loving respect a child has for a good father. His mercy carries on from parents to children, age after age. God showed this mercy most of all in sending his Son.

God's "arm" stands for his great power. He scatters proud people like wind blowing chaff. Often their own proud plans turn against them. Mary speaks of what God would do through the Messiah as if it were already done.

God brings proud rulers down and lifts up lowly people. History does not turn by luck but by God's wise and fair rule. One example is God removing Saul and raising up David the shepherd boy. God did the same in the gospel when he chose humble fishermen to carry his message.

God feeds the needy who come to him, both with daily bread and with spiritual gifts. Those who know their need of Christ he fills with the best things. Those who feel rich and think they need nothing, trusting in themselves, go away empty.
